security_audit.summary: The 142 static alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, signed descriptor data, and defensive installer operations. However, native publisher signature checks are disabled for macOS and Windows binaries, creating a high-severity supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: macOS and Windows installers accept binaries without enforced native publisher signatures.
remediation.suggestion: Require notarized Apple signatures and valid Authenticode signatures with pinned publisher identities before installation. Reject releases whose signature status is deferred or unverified.

The quoted uname substitution selects the standard per-user installation directory. It does not evaluate untrusted text as a command.
The substitution passes the quoted target directory through printf and tr to reject control characters. It is defensive validation without shell evaluation.
The quoted ls command records the installation directory inode for a later race check. Its path argument is quoted and not treated as code.
The substitution computes the existing executable SHA-256 through a fixed helper. The quoted path cannot alter the invoked command.
The substitution creates a private temporary directory under the validated target directory. The template is quoted and no command text is user-controlled.
The substitution measures the downloaded archive with fixed wc and tr commands. The archive path is quoted and not evaluated as shell syntax.
The substitution computes the downloaded archive SHA-256 for comparison with a pinned digest. The quoted path cannot select another command.
The substitution lists archive entries with tar so the script can enforce an exact allowlist before extraction. The archive path is quoted.
The substitution hashes the extracted executable and compares it with a pinned digest. The quoted path is not evaluated as command text.
The quoted uname substitution gates macOS verification logic. It uses a fixed command and does not evaluate untrusted input.
The substitution reads the candidate's macOS signing authority using fixed verification tools. The candidate path is quoted and the result is only compared.
The quoted ls command verifies that the target directory inode did not change during download. This is a defensive race-condition check.
The substitution rehashes the existing target before replacement to detect concurrent changes. It invokes a fixed helper with a quoted path.
The URL is the fixed HTTPS origin for a versioned PersonWise release. The installer also verifies exact artifact size and SHA-256 digest before installation.
The path is the conventional per-user XDG binary directory. Access is limited to installing the approved PersonWise executable without elevated privileges.
The path is the conventional per-user .local/bin directory on non-Linux Unix systems. It is expected installer behavior and does not access unrelated hidden data.
The hidden name is a unique installer work directory, not an attempt to conceal persistence. It is removed by the script's exit trap.
The redirection to /dev/null only suppresses output while checking for sha256sum. It neither reads sensitive device data nor writes persistent files.
The redirection to /dev/null only suppresses output while checking for shasum. It neither reads sensitive device data nor writes persistent files.
mktemp creates a unique private work directory under the validated installation directory, and a trap removes it. This limits race and cleanup risks.
The hard link performs a no-overwrite atomic install after validation and fails if the target exists. The source and target are both bounded installer paths.

content.value_statement: Internal change communications often leave employees uncertain about timelines, responsibilities, and support. This skill converts approved materials into an interactive, grounded adoption course.
actual_capabilities: Structures approved change communications into a role-focused course covering reasons, impacts, timelines, support, and knowledge checks.
Creates interactive digital-human courses through the PersonWise CLI and browser-based authentication.
Uploads user-selected source documents and tracks their processing status before course generation continues.
Reviews outlines, scripts, images, and run checkpoints against source evidence and course requirements.
Supports private delivery, link access, publication, and Topics submission when the user authorizes the requested target.
Resumes, repairs, refines, and queries existing PersonWise course runs using current service state.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI 1.1.6 or newer, browser authentication, a PersonWise account, network access, and available course credits.
Cannot add facts about personnel decisions, dates, scope, or future states unless approved sources support them.
Course size and creation depend on live account limits, source processing, and service availability.
The bundled installers currently lack enforced native publisher signature verification on macOS and Windows.

use_cases.title: Prepare Employees for a Reorganization
use_cases.description: Convert approved leadership communications into a private course explaining reasons, role impacts, timing, and support channels.

use_cases.title: Train Teams on a New Process
use_cases.description: Create a source-grounded course that shows changed responsibilities, expected actions, and escalation paths for each affected team.

use_cases.title: Support an Internal Software Rollout
use_cases.description: Build an interactive rollout course covering the implementation timeline, employee tasks, training resources, and approved answers to common questions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Adoption Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private internal change adoption course from [source materials]. Explain why the change is happening, what employees must do, and where support is available.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with approved communications and no detailed format requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Tailor Training by Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [page count]-page adoption course for [audience]. Separate impacts for [roles] and include the approved timeline, support channels, and a short knowledge check.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for role-specific employee training.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Materials-Only Rollout Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only the attached rollout documents to create a private course. Flag unsupported or conflicting claims, preserve every source, and route open questions to [channel].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request requiring strict source control and ambiguity handling.

prompt_templates.title: Resume and Publish a Reviewed Course
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume PersonWise run [run ID]. Review the latest outline, script, and images against the approved sources. Fix objective issues, complete the run, then enable [access mode].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow involving durable state, checkpoint review, and authorized publication.

output_examples.input: Create a private course from our approved reorganization memo for all affected employees.
output: A concise course explains the approved reason for the reorganization and separates confirmed role impacts from open decisions.
A timeline shows communicated milestones, employee actions, and named support channels.
The final result includes a private, login-required course link and verified run status.

output_examples.input: Build a five-page adoption course for our new expense process using only the attached policy.
output: Five pages cover the process purpose, changed steps, employee responsibilities, timing, support, and a short self-check.
Unsupported exceptions are excluded, and unclear policy points are marked for the finance team.

output_examples.input: Update our existing rollout course and share it with anyone who has the link.
output_examples.output: The course is reviewed against current sources, updated with supported corrections, published with link access, and returned with a verified playable URL.

best_practices: Provide final, approved communications and identify the affected audiences before course creation.
State the desired page count, language, and access mode, or accept the private default.
Review flagged ambiguities and route employee-specific questions to an authorized manager, HR contact, or change team.
anti_patterns: Do not request assurances about layoffs, roles, dates, or outcomes that approved sources do not support.
Do not upload files that the user did not select without disclosing the exact file and obtaining approval.
Do not describe private editor links as public share links or claim Topics submission means approval.

faq.question: What source materials should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide approved change announcements, timelines, process documents, training resources, and support contacts relevant to the affected employees.

faq.question: Can the skill create content without documents?
faq.answer: Yes, for topic-based courses. For company-specific claims, approved materials remain necessary to prevent unsupported statements.

faq.question: Does the course answer employee questions?
faq.answer: Yes. The digital-human format supports voice questions grounded in course content and routes unsupported individual questions to named channels.

faq.question: Is the finished course public by default?
faq.answer: No. The skill defaults to private access unless the user requests link access, publication, or Topics submission.

faq.question: What does the PersonWise account require?
faq.answer: It requires browser authentication, available course credits, supported account limits, and access to the PersonWise service.

faq.question: Can the skill update an existing course?
faq.answer: Yes. It can resume, repair, refine, publish, change access, or query an existing course when current service state permits.
